Build a Flow View for the Supply Line Monitor app.



Add a new file ui/flow_view.py that implements a FlowView(QWidget) class using QPainter for rendering. This is a wiring diagram / transit map style view showing global supply routes as straight horizontal and vertical lines (right-angle bends only, no curves), coloured by commodity type, with animated icons/packets sliding along them. It should feel like a Bloomberg terminal meets a London Tube map meets a PCB schematic.



Visual Style:



Background: #0a1119 (very dark navy)

Subtle dot-grid pattern drawn underneath everything (like engineering paper)

Route lines: 3px solid, colour coded by commodity (see below)

A soft glow effect behind each line (wider, lower opacity version of the same line drawn first)

Stop nodes: filled circles, border colour = route status colour

Animated packets: small rotating diamonds sliding along the lines, colour matches the route

Labels: uppercase, monospace font (Courier New or Consolas), small, clean

Status colours: #39ff88 normal, #f0c040 watch, #ff4422 disrupted, #8a9ab0 no data

Commodity colours:



Oil: #cc2200

Grain: #f0a500

Containers: #2255cc

LNG: #44aaff

Air: #9effd9

Fishing: #6fdcff

Rare Earth: #c78bff

Layout Logic:



The diagram should be laid out in 3 logical columns:



Left column (~15% from left edge): Origin nodes (Persian Gulf, Black Sea, US Gulf, East Asia, Australia, Indian Ocean)

Middle column(s) (~40-60% from left): Chokepoint/waypoint stop nodes (Hormuz, Suez, Bosphorus, Malacca, Bab-el-Mandeb, Panama)

Right column (~85% from left): Destination nodes (Europe, Asia/China, N. America, Global, SE Asia)

Routes run LEFT → RIGHT. If two routes share a chokepoint, the lines should converge on the same stop node for that chokepoint. Lines exit origin nodes horizontally, bend vertically to align with their chokepoints, then continue horizontally to destinations. All bends are 90 degrees only.



Each route is defined as a list of stops in order, e.g.:

Animation:



Use a QTimer firing every 50ms

Each route has one animated packet (a small 8x8 rotated square / diamond shape)

Each packet has a progress float (0.0 → 1.0) that advances by 0.002 per tick

Position is interpolated along the route's list of node positions (straight lines between consecutive stops, with right-angle bends — go horizontal first, then vertical to reach the next node)

When progress hits 1.0 it resets to 0.0

The diamond is filled with the route colour and has a small white border

Disrupted routes: packet flashes (alternate opacity every 4 ticks) and the line uses a dashed pattern

Interactivity:



Click on any node (stop circle): Emit a signal node_clicked(str) with the node name. The parent window should handle this by showing the info panel.

Click on any route line (within 8px): Emit route_clicked(str) with the route id. Highlight that route (make its line 5px wide and fully bright) and dim all others to 30% opacity for 3 seconds then reset.

Hover over a node: Show a QToolTip with the node name and current risk level

Right-click on a route: Show a context menu with "Ask Grok about this route" option — emit grok_requested(str) signal with route id

Info Panel (build as a separate class FlowInfoPanel(QWidget) in the same file): A panel that slides in from the right (or just appears — no need for fancy animation) when a node or route is clicked. Shows:



Route/node name at the top (large, bold)

Current status with colour

List of stops in order with their status indicators

"Ask Grok 🤖" button — emits grok_requested(str)

"View on Map 🗺️" button — emits view_on_map(str)

Close button (X) top right

Import FlowView and FlowInfoPanel

Use a QStackedWidget to switch between MapView (index 0), FlowView (index 1), and a placeholder QLabel("🌐 Globe View — Coming Soon") (index 2)

When FlowView emits grok_requested(route_id), switch to the Grok tab in the side panel and pre-fill the route selector with that route

When FlowView emits view_on_map(route_id), switch to Map View and call map_view.highlight_route(route_id)

The FlowView should call set_route_status(route_id, status) when route statuses are updated by the polling worker

def set_all_statuses(self, statuses: dict[str, str]) -> None: ...

def get_route_ids(self) -> list[str]: ...

Do NOT modify map/map.html, services/, workers/, database/, or config/. Only touch ui/flow_view.py (create it) and ui/main_window.py (modify it to add the view toggle and QStackedWidget).

def ask_grok_about_alert(self, alert) -> GrokResponse:

    """

    Called automatically when a WARNING or CRITICAL alert fires.

    Asks Grok to search X and news for context on the specific alert.

    Cheaper model used to keep costs down.

    """

    query = (

        f"A supply chain disruption alert has just been detected:\n"

        f"Title: {alert.title}\n"

        f"Location: {alert.location or 'Unknown'}\n"

        f"Commodity: {alert.commodity or 'Unknown'}\n"

        f"Severity: {alert.severity}\n\n"

        f"Please search X/Twitter and recent news for posts related to this event "

        f"in the last 3 hours. Summarise: what is happening, which supply routes "

        f"are affected, what chokepoints are involved, estimated market impact, "

        f"and risk level (low/medium/high/critical). Be concise — max 200 words."

    )

    # Force grok-3-mini for auto-triggered queries to keep cost minimal

    return self._call_grok(query, model_override="grok-3-mini")

Make sure _call_grok accepts an optional model_override parameter that takes priority over the settings value.
